metaData.originalTitle: I/O ‘26 news for agent developers on Google Cloud
metaData.title: I/O '26 news for agent developers on Google Cloud
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Google Cloud unveils a unified agent development toolkit at I/O '26, featuring Antigravity 2.0, Managed Agents API, and ADK 2.0, structured across a four-rung spectrum from low-code to code-first.
metaData.summary: This article from the Google Cloud Blog details the new agent development tools and platform updates announced at Google I/O '26. The core of the announcement is a unified development toolkit built on the A2A protocol, structured as a four-rung ladder of choice. The rungs are: 1) Agent Studio for low-code visual agent building, 2) the new Managed Agents API for a configuration-first, agent-as-a-service approach, 3) Antigravity 2.0 and its CLI for developer-focused coding and agent orchestration, and 4) the Agent Development Kit (ADK 2.0) for full code-first control. The article emphasizes that these rungs are additive and interoperable, allowing teams to start fast and scale to deeper customization. It also highlights the platform's openness, supporting integration with other coding agents like Claude Code, and provides a practical 'what to try first' guide for developers, covering exploration, building, governance, evaluation, and security.
metaData.featuredReason: A developer-oriented breakdown of Google Cloud's new agent stack. It organizes Agent Studio, Managed Agents API, Antigravity 2.0, and ADK 2.0 into a clear ladder from low-code configuration to code-first control, making it useful for teams deciding how much abstraction, governance, and customization their agent projects need.

mainPoints.point: Google Cloud introduces a four-rung spectrum for building agents, from low-code to code-first.
mainPoints.explanation: The spectrum includes Agent Studio (low-code), Managed Agents API (configuration-first), Antigravity 2.0 (developer-focused orchestration), and ADK 2.0 (code-first). All rungs are built on the A2A protocol for interoperability.

mainPoints.point: The new Managed Agents API offers an agent-as-a-service model with a secure-by-design sandbox.
mainPoints.explanation: This API allows developers to define agentic behavior and let Google Cloud handle infrastructure. The agent runs in an ephemeral sandbox, and integration with A2A and platform governance is forthcoming.

mainPoints.point: Antigravity 2.0 is a new standalone desktop app for orchestrating coding agents, with a companion CLI.
mainPoints.explanation: Antigravity 2.0 provides a centralized workspace for complex tasks like refactoring and test generation. The CLI offers the same capabilities in a terminal environment, and both can be used with enterprise security via Cloud OAuth.

mainPoints.point: ADK 2.0 introduces a unified graph-based engine and collaborative workflows for building custom agent meshes.
mainPoints.explanation: ADK 2.0 is for engineers who want full code control. It features dynamic workflows, a collaborative API for self-managing agent teams, and expanded language support including Kotlin.

mainPoints.point: The platform is designed for openness, integrating with other coding agents like Claude Code.
mainPoints.explanation: Google Cloud provides tools like the Agent CLI and ADK to work with various agents, allowing developers to keep their preferred interfaces while running inference on Google Cloud's secure infrastructure.

keyQuotes: We like to think of the agent development ecosystem as four rungs on a ladder, designed to give you a clear slider between out-of-the-box configuration and complete code-first control.
Underneath all four rungs is the A2A protocol. This interoperability ensures that an agent built on the first rung can be called as a sub-agent on the fourth rung.

Pick the rung that fits the project. Bring whatever coding agent your team prefers. The platform you graduate to is the same one either way, and the data stays inside your Cloud project the whole time.
If Managed Agents are configuration-first, ADK is engineering-first.
The graph model is worth the learning curve as soon as you have more than two branching paths.

relatedArticles.title: TPU 8t and TPU 8i technical deep dive
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a detailed technical overview of Google's eighth-generation TPU systems, TPU 8t and TPU 8i, explaining their specialized architectures for large-scale training and high-concurrency inference respectively, and the performance gains they offer.

relatedArticles.title: Using AI as a Thinking Partner for Large-Scale Engineering Systems
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A Google Senior Staff Engineer shares a structured methodology for using AI as a thinking partner to understand, experiment with, and redesign a complex, multi-language, multi-repository engineering system.

relatedArticles.title: Gemini Embedding 2: Our first natively multimodal embedding model
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Google introduces Gemini Embedding 2, its first natively multimodal embedding model that unifies text, image, video, audio, and documents into a single semantic space for advanced RAG and search.

relatedArticles.title: Ultimate prompting guide for Nano Banana
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This technical guide details the capabilities and prompting frameworks for Google's Nano Banana image models, focusing on real-time search integration and professional creative controls.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI Agents SDK Gains New Capabilities for Long-Running Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces new capabilities in its Agents SDK for building long-running agents with enhanced control over execution, including sandboxed runs and customizable memory management.

relatedArticles.title: Memory and Dreaming for Self-Learning Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic introduces Memory and Dreaming, two new primitives for its Managed Agents API, enabling agents to achieve continuous self-learning by managing their own knowledge in a file system-like structure and asynchronously curating that knowledge to improve over time.

relatedArticles.title: Google Cloud Next 2026 Wrap Up
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Google Cloud Next '26 unveiled a comprehensive suite of agentic enterprise products, including the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, 8th-gen TPUs, and the Agentic Data Cloud, marking a major shift from pilot to production in the AI era.

relatedArticles.title: From "Vibe Checks" to Continuous Evaluation: Engineering Reliable AI Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a comprehensive engineering framework for transitioning AI agent development from subjective 'vibe checks' to a rigorous, automated continuous evaluation (CE) workflow.

relatedArticles.title: Innovations from Google I/O 26 on Google Cloud
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Google I/O 26 announces a suite of new AI models and platform updates for Google Cloud, including Gemini 3.5 Flash, Gemini Omni, the Antigravity platform, and the Gemini Spark personal agent, all aimed at powering the Agentic Enterprise.

relatedArticles.title: All the news from the Google I/O 2026 Developer keynote
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Google I/O 2026 Developer keynote announces Gemini 3.5 models, the Antigravity 2.0 agent platform, and new tools for building Android and web apps with AI agents.
